exposure: First-trimester transabdominal ultrasonographic placenta previa diagnosis
posterior placenta in the first trimester
outcome: Placenta previa persistence into the second trimester
cohort: The study included 185 patients with singleton pregnancies who received a first-trimester transabdominal ultrasonographic diagnosis of placenta previa between January and December 2022.
finding: First-trimester transabdominal ultrasonographic placenta previa diagnosis has a poor predictive capacity for its persistence to the second trimester (14.0%) and an even lower capacity for persistence to delivery (1.6%).
mod_finding: Prior cesarean delivery was not identified as a risk factor for placenta previa persistence to the second trimester.
